title: Personal factors: age, gender, education, tenure and more
summary: How age, education, gender, tenure, creativity, marital status and dependents relate to work outcomes.

chunks.heading: Age and education
chunks.explanation_md:
**Age** is linked with several outcomes: **performance**, **satisfaction level** (a positive link, but it can be reversed due to change in technology), **turnover**, **adaptability** and **absenteeism** (avoidable and unavoidable types).

**Education** is linked with increased positive outcomes. The slide also contrasts **general vs specialised education**.

**Abilities** come in two kinds: **intellectual** and **physical** (covered in the next topics).
chunks.exam_line: Age relates to performance, satisfaction (positive link, can reverse with technology change), turnover, adaptability and absenteeism. Education relates to increased positive outcomes.

check_questions.stem: The positive link between age and satisfaction can be reversed because of what?

chunks.heading: Gender: men and women
chunks.explanation_md:
On **job performance**, the assumption on the slide is that there is **no significant difference in job productivity** between men and women.

**Psychological studies** say women are more willing to conform to authority and men are more aggressive in having expectations of success.

The slide also lists **preference of work schedules** and **absence and turnover rates** as areas where men and women are compared.
chunks.exam_line: Assumption: no significant difference in job productivity between men and women. Psychological studies: women more willing to conform to authority; men more aggressive in expecting success.

check_questions.stem: What does the slide assume about job productivity of men and women?
Psychological studies on the slide say women are more willing to conform to authority.

chunks.heading: Tenure
chunks.explanation_md:
**Tenure** (seniority) shows these links:
- Seniority is **negatively related to absence**.
- Seniority is **negatively related to turnover**.
- Tenure on one's previous job is a **powerful predictor of future turnover**.
- Tenure is **positively related to satisfaction**.

key_terms.meaning: Length of time on the job (seniority): negatively related to absence and turnover, positively related to satisfaction.

chunks.exam_line: Tenure: negatively related to absence and turnover, positively related to satisfaction; previous-job tenure predicts future turnover.

Tenure on one's previous job is a powerful predictor of future ____.

chunks.heading: Creativity, marital status and dependents
chunks.explanation_md:
**Creativity**: creative individuals have at least three categories of attributes: **background experience**, **personal traits** (open-minded, high energy, self-confidence) and **cognitive abilities** (power to think intelligently and analyse situations and data effectively).

**Marital status**: married people have fewer absences, less turnover and are more satisfied.

**Number of dependents**: has an impact on absenteeism and on satisfaction.

key_terms.meaning: Background experience, personal traits (open-minded, high energy, self-confidence) and cognitive abilities.

chunks.exam_line: Creative people have background experience, personal traits and cognitive abilities. Married people: fewer absences, less turnover, more satisfied.

questions.stem: Explain the relationship between tenure and work outcomes.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Tenure** (seniority) is **negatively related to absence** and **negatively related to turnover**. It is **positively related to satisfaction**. Tenure on one's previous job is a powerful predictor of future turnover.

So a manager can expect long-serving employees to be absent less and leave less often.

questions.stem: Explain how age and education relate to work behaviour.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Age** is linked with performance, satisfaction level, turnover, adaptability and absenteeism (avoidable and unavoidable types). The positive link between age and satisfaction can be reversed due to change in technology.

**Education** is linked with increased positive outcomes, and the slide contrasts general versus specialised education.

rubric.point: Age linked to performance, turnover, adaptability
Age and satisfaction positive but can reverse with technology

questions.stem: Discuss the personal factors affecting individual behaviour, including gender, marital status and creativity.
questions.model_answer_md:
Personal factors include age, gender, education, abilities, marital status, number of dependents, creativity and emotional intelligence.

**Age**: linked with performance, satisfaction (positive but can reverse with technology change), turnover, adaptability and absenteeism.

**Gender**: the assumption is no significant difference in job productivity between men and women. Psychological studies say women are more willing to conform to authority and men more aggressive in expecting success. Men and women are also compared on work schedule preferences and absence and turnover rates.

**Marital status**: married people have fewer absences, less turnover and more satisfaction. **Number of dependents** affects absenteeism and satisfaction.

**Tenure**: negatively related to absence and turnover, positively to satisfaction.

**Creativity**: needs background experience, personal traits (open-mindedness, energy, self-confidence) and cognitive abilities.

Conclusion: these factors shape behaviour and managers should consider them in decisions.
